contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageSummary: Grind size changes everything about your cup. Here's how to match it to your brewer, and what to adjust when the taste is off.
contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageText:
If your coffee tastes sour or bitter, the beans usually aren't the problem — the grind is. Water pulls flavor out faster from fine grounds and slower from coarse ones, so the right size depends on how long your coffee and water spend together.

A quick guide

  • Espresso: fine, like powdered sugar
  • V60 and other pour-overs: medium-fine, like table salt
  • Chemex: medium-coarse, like rough sand
  • French press and cold brew: coarse, like sea salt

Taste and adjust

Sour, thin, or salty? Go finer. Bitter, dry, or harsh? Go coarser. Change one step at a time and keep everything else the same, and you'll find your sweet spot within a few brews.

A good burr grinder makes this a lot easier. Blade grinders chop unevenly, so you get a mix of dust and boulders in every batch.
